newsitem.title: UK: UK to participate fully in TARGET - BOE.
newsitem.headline: UK to participate fully in TARGET - BOE.

text.p: Britain will participate fully in the planned single European currency payments system, whether or not it joins monetary union, a Bank of England official said.
There has been disagreement among EU states over whether countries outside EMU should have access to the Trans-European Automated Real-Time Gross Settlement Express Transfer (TARGET).
Some, such as Germany, are unhappy about giving full access to intraday liquidity to those outside the single currency.
"We remain keen to see TARGET developed as an attractive payments system, for all users in the EU, including those in the UK," said Bank of England executive director Ian Plenderleith.

If the UK is in EMU, the present sterling system will become a euro system but those banks and their customers who want to continue making sterling payments will be able to do so, Plenderleith told a conference in London.

If the UK is out, the euro would be treated as another foreign currency: the present sterling system would continue but facilities for national real-time gross settlement systems (RTGS) in euro would be developed to run in parallel.

"In or out, our RTGS euro facilities will link into TARGET, and we are already making good progress with building the necessary linkage as a full participant in the TARGET project," Plenderleith said.
